title: PEPIC identifies a BHET-hydrolyzing enzyme candidate
summary: PEPIC is a sequence-based convolutional model that predicts PET-hydrolyzing potential. The study reports prioritizing W2061_PET9 and experimentally showing that purified protein converts soluble BHET into MHET, confirmed by HPLC and mass spectrometry. The experiment used a soluble PET intermediate; it does not establish degradation of polymer PET. Homology screening and human selection also contributed.

evidence.tested: Purified W2061_PET9 converted BHET to MHET in an in-vitro assay confirmed chromatographically and by mass spectrometry.
evidence.unknown: Polymer PET degradation, exact sequence-level prior characterization and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: PEPIC scores sequences for predicted PET-hydrolytic activity to prioritize a candidate after genomic/homology selection; direct assay validates soluble BHET turnover.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher PDF indexed full text confirms title/DOI, publication date, AI role and Fig. 6 experimental validation.
